speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing this rash on your scalp and forehead, and does it itch or burn?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history; the seasonal worsening and family history are important clues. Has the rash spread to any other areas of the body like the hands, feet, or diaper area? Also, to better assess the severity, I need to see the affected skin.

REQUEST IMAGES: Scalp and forehead close-up.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis (Infantile Cradle Cap with Facial Involvement).

The combination of greasy yellow scales, erythematous patches on the scalp and forehead, worsening in cold weather, and a family history of psoriasis is highly characteristic of seborrheic dermatitis rather than psoriasis in an infant. The symptoms described are classic for this condition.
